relevance.rationale: *** WRONG JOIN ***. The seeded id points at a single-author 1988 topological-quantum-field-theory entry. The document is a THREE-author paper on the monodromy of the Hitchin connection, deposited in the French HAL archive and later published in a geometry-and-physics journal; its identifiers, authorship and decade all differ from the seeded entry. id set to null (greps for all three author surnames and for the HAL handle in references.ts are empty). On its own merits the document proves that the image of the monodromy representation of the Hitchin connection on the sheaf of generalized SL(2) theta functions, over a family of smooth projective curves of genus at least 3, contains an element of infinite order. The folio uses Hitchin-adjacent language in its q-geometric-Langlands chapter, but that chapter is about q-opers and q-Hecke eigensheaves; no block asks whether the Hitchin monodromy image is infinite, and there is no consumer for this result. Tangential: adjacent field, no consumer here. Scope-(a) against the corpus as it stands. SEPARATE FINDING ON THE SEEDED KEY, from the corpus side: witten1988 splits in citation quality - see proposedActions.

proposedActions.rationale: If the q-geometric-Langlands chapter ever needs the classical (q=1) Hitchin-connection monodromy statement as a comparison point, this is the source; today there is no consumer, so registering it is optional rather than required. Recorded so the document is not re-triaged from scratch.

witten1988 is cited at QOU/MassDerivation.lean:170 and QOU/Calculations.lean:142 on lemmas quantum_planck_approx and h_q_value_in_unit_interval, labelled '- Quantum Planck derivation'. Those lemmas are arithmetic facts about the literal hbar_q = 1 - 1/q at q = 1.1097, closed by norm_num; Witten's TQFT paper contains no hbar_q and derives nothing about it. The citation is decorative at those two sites (it is load-bearing at the genuine TQFT/Chern-Simons sites: models-of-qous/categorical-action-vs-chern-simons.md, quantum-observable-universes/reeb-su2.lean, categorical-reeb*.lean, Glossary.lean). Record the split and drop or re-source the two Quantum-Planck sites.
